_note: #1093 R1 + #1111 + #1092 + #1129 — set B, VERSIONED WITH THE RULES (13 files: top p1..p9, bottom p1..p4). The programs both jobs post under the one naming rule, #1111’s canonical owned order with the ball reach-margin gate, and #1092’s two-space rest rule. vs tableVersion 1092-1: 9 of 13 contents identical; #1129 changed the four ball-finish programs — top p7/p8 and bottom p3/p4 — because the row sampler’s floor is now a sampling spacing, min(step-over/10, 0.05 mm) floored at the chord tolerance (0.005 mm), instead of the chord tolerance itself, and the edge-contact search stops at a 1e-3 mm interval (see changedSince1092-1). top p7/p8 are surface-identical on a 0.5 mm raster (max |Δz| 0.0000 mm on 4 800 / 3 850 shared cells, 0 cells off by > 0.01 mm); bottom p3/p4 differ on 591 / 195 of 14 338 / 14 079 shared cells, every changed cell on the shallower side (max 0.646 / 3.299 mm at cells straddling walls; 172 / 10 cells > 0.1 mm), and never deeper. Every program’s goal verdict is unchanged: pass, adjudicated max 0.000 mm, 0 over-relief cells, 0 cut-into; the goal sentence moved only on the bottom (98.4 → 98.2 % of the goal within 0.01 mm; the top reads 96.4 % both). The 2026-11-07 deltas (#1080’s top p7/p8, #1111’s top p6 25 mm O-flute and the bottom’s 5→4 programs) stay recorded in changedSince20261107. The e2e reads this table as the cross-door check.
rule: #1111 (0f comment 6729368477): (a) the canonical owned order — tier (inv: → user: → cat: → built-in), then key — so both doors see one list; (b) the ball tie needs the reach-margin gate (flute − deepest cut ≥ reach.marginMm, recommendation 1.0 mm) while any candidate passes, and a remaining tie falls to the key, printed "by key, pending #1114"; (c) the sequence primary, the curved rough's flat and the rest ball keep their pre-#1111 order under the canonical order, stated as "same diameter: by key, pending #1114" — WITHIN THIS RULE the bottom posts 4 programs (rough + pocket on the 25 mm O-flute) and the top 9. Which cutter among equals a plan SHOULD prefer is the open policy issue #1114 (stiffness vs reach vs bit changes vs time), with three measured plans as evidence. (d) #1092 (cam, 0f's two-space rule): a rest cuts material work and CL-space centres — its floor mask is already cutter-centre space (no radius inset); a rest cuts only a floor the cutter belongs on, and a one-cell sliver is not a floor.

facedJobCardRename._note: A FACED job’s uploaded names changed with #1093 too: the release store now names programs by the one naming function, as Save all, the sheet and the CLI already did. No set B file is affected (set B has no facing). An operator who cut a faced job from an older build sees the skim’s name change on the card; re-uploading under the new names is the one-time step.
facedJobCardRename.old: <stem>-p1.nc = the skim; <stem>-p2.nc … = the engravings (cut-order numbering, skim included)
facedJobCardRename.new: <stem>-face.nc = the skim; <stem>-p1.nc … = the engravings (numbered among themselves; one engraving = <stem>.nc)
facedJobCardRename.dryRun: <stem>-dry-face.nc for a lifted skim; <stem>-dry-p1.nc … for lifted engravings
